title: Compact legend inline summaries, touch-friendly scrubbing, and WCAG contrast audit for time-series
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Our time-series charts currently show verbose legends that consume UI space and perform poorly on mobile. Tooltips/skimming rely on hover interactions which are not available on touch devices. Additionally, several color combinations in the current token palette fail WCAG 2.1 AA contrast for users with low vision or common color deficiencies.

Goal: Introduce a compact legend mode that shows inline numeric summaries (current, delta, and mini-spark) per series, add a robust touch-friendly scrubbing and tooltip pattern for mobile, and run a WCAG contrast and color-blindness audit with corrective token updates. The solution must be performant (minimal re-renders, virtualization for long series lists), compatible with existing API props, and configurable via design tokens.

Scope: UI patterns (compact legend layout, collapsed legend states), interaction patterns (touch scrub, long-press details, accessible keyboard fallbacks), visual tokens update (palette and semantic token mapping), and perf patterns (canvas rendering fallback, memoized selectors). Excludes backend telemetry changes and large-scale telemetry dashboarding (handled in ENG-2923).
acceptance_criteria:
- Compact legend component available as <Legend compact> boolean prop that swaps the full legend for a condensed row per series showing: label, numeric current value, delta (colored), and a 24px sparkline thumbnail.
- Touch scrub interaction works on iOS and Android: tap-and-drag on chart updates inline summary values and shows a persistent summary bubble; long-press pins the scrub state.
- Keyboard users can focus legend items and use arrow keys to step through scrub states; focus order documented.
- All updated color combinations pass WCAG 2.1 AA contrast for text and UI elements; a color-blindness palette variant is provided (deuteranopia-friendly).
- Perf: rendering of charts with >100 series maintains interactive frame rate (>30fps on mid-range mobile) through virtualization and memoization strategies; automated perf harness demonstrates improvements vs baseline.
- API/back-compat: existing props remain supported; new props are opt-in and documented in the design system storybook.
- Design tokens: new semantic tokens created (chart.series.label, chart.series.delta.positive, chart.series.delta.negative, chart.legend.sparkline.background) and documented for engineering consumption.
design_notes:
- Prototype: compact legend reduces vertical footprint by collapsing series rows; hover reveals contextual controls (pin, mute). For mobile the controls are via an overflow menu.
- Sparkline thumbnails are rendered as inline SVG by default; fallback to canvas for large-scale lists (virtualized). We recommend 2px stroke, rounded caps to align with tokens.
- Contrast: run tokens through ColorSafe and a11y tools; selected candidate palette attached.
- Motion: scrub bubble should respect reduced-motion preference.
- Token naming: prefer semantic (chart.*) rather than raw hex tokens to allow runtime theming.
- Edge case: when series labels overflow the compact row we truncate with ellipsis and expose full label in the pinned detail view.
engineering_notes:
- Performance plan: memoize legend rows via React.memo + stable keying; batch updates during scrubbing using requestAnimationFrame; consider using OffscreenCanvas for server-side generation of sparks.
- Virtualization: use windowing for legend lists >20 items.
- Touch interaction: implement pointer events to unify mouse/touch; avoid 300ms delays; provide passive listeners.
- Accessibility: ensure ARIA role="list" for legend, role="listitem" for rows; add aria-live region updates for scrub value changes; provide text-only summary alternative.
- Back-compat: default behavior unchanged; export new compact legend as opt-in.
- Metrics: add perf testing scenario in Lighthouse and optional telemetry flag in ENG-2923 for load testing.
